agree.reason: A director who thinks this is the usual yearly complaint gets an average loss figure and general asks, but no invoices to check, no meeting date and no specific contract term she could act on, so she has little reason to change her view.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'third will close within a year' claim and says plainly that the cause of the nine closures is unknown, but 'wait for mail order, or go without' and the add-on demand for PBM rate disclosure go somewhat beyond what the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: It never works out the obvious derived figure, about $5,580 a year lost at the writer's own pharmacy (3,100 × $1.80), or scales the loss across the 22% share, so the numbers stay raw and abstract.

right_comparison.reason: It says rural members would 'drive much farther' but leaves out that the nearest chain is more than 20 miles away and that two pharmacies will stop filling for plan members, so the real alternative to doing nothing stays vague.

qualification.reason: The hedge about the closures is honest but gives the reader nothing to check, with no number, deadline or consequence such as 'two pharmacies stop filling plan prescriptions on July 1 unless...'.

objections.reason: The 'you complain every year' objection goes unanswered because the offer to share invoices is left out, and the 'plenty of chains' objection is only half met because the 20-mile fact is missing.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter suited to both the plan and the newspapers, though it uses placeholders for the alliance name and signer even though those were known, and its ask leaves out the fill fee.
